Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From 4007844b05815717f522c7ea9914e24ad0ff6c79 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Nicolas Boichat <drinkcat@chromium.org>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2020 11:31:35 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] soc: mediatek: Check if power domains can be powered on at
 boot time

In the error case, where a power domain cannot be powered on
successfully at boot time (in mtk_register_power_domains),
pm_genpd_init would still be called with is_off=false, and the
system would later try to disable the power domain again, triggering
warnings as disabled clocks are disabled again (and other potential
issues).

Also print a warning splat in that case, as this should never
happen.

Fixes: c84e358718a66f7 ("soc: Mediatek: Add SCPSYS power domain driver")
Signed-off-by: Nicolas Boichat <drinkcat@chromium.org>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20200928113107.v2.1.I5e6f8c262031d0451fe7241b744f4f3111c1ce71@changeid
Signed-off-by: Matthias Brugger <matthias.bgg@gmail.com>

diff --git a/drivers/soc/mediatek/mtk-scpsys.c b/drivers/soc/mediatek/mtk-scpsys.c
index f669d3754627..ca75b14931ec 100644
--- a/drivers/soc/mediatek/mtk-scpsys.c
+++ b/drivers/soc/mediatek/mtk-scpsys.c
@@ -524,6 +524,7 @@ static void mtk_register_power_domains(struct platform_device *pdev,
 	for (i = 0; i < num; i++) {
 		struct scp_domain *scpd = &scp->domains[i];
 		struct generic_pm_domain *genpd = &scpd->genpd;
+		bool on;
 
 		/*
 		 * Initially turn on all domains to make the domains usable
@@ -531,9 +532,9 @@ static void mtk_register_power_domains(struct platform_device *pdev,
 		 * software.  The unused domains will be switched off during
 		 * late_init time.
 		 */
-		genpd->power_on(genpd);
+		on = !WARN_ON(genpd->power_on(genpd) < 0);
 
-		pm_genpd_init(genpd, NULL, false);
+		pm_genpd_init(genpd, NULL, !on);
 	}
 
 	/*
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/soc/mediatek/mtk-scpsys.c`**
1. A new boolean variable `on` is introduced to track whether the power domain was successfully powered on.
2. The call to `genpd->power_on(genpd)` is modified to check for errors. If it fails (returns a negative value), a warning is triggered using `WARN_ON`, and `on` is set to false.
3. The call to `pm_genpd_init` is updated to use the value of `on`. If `on` is true (indicating the power domain was successfully powered on), it passes `true` to `pm_genpd_init`; otherwise, it passes `false`.

### Relationships Between Modifications
The modifications are related in that they address a specific error handling scenario during the initialization of power domains. The introduction of the `on` variable allows the code to determine if the power domain was successfully powered on before proceeding to initialize it with `pm_genpd_init`. This change prevents the system from attempting to disable a power domain that failed to power on, which could lead to warnings and other potential issues. The overall goal is to enhance the robustness of the power domain management during boot time.

Here is the commit message:
soc: mediatek: Check if power domains can be powered on at
 boot time

In the error case, where a power domain cannot be powered on
successfully at boot time (in mtk_register_power_domains),
pm_genpd_init would still be called with is_off=false, and the
system would later try to disable the power domain again, triggering
warnings as disabled clocks are disabled again (and other potential
issues).

Also print a warning splat in that case, as this should never
happen.

Fixes: c84e358718a66f7 ("soc: Mediatek: Add SCPSYS power domain driver")
Signed-off-by: Nicolas Boichat <drinkcat@chromium.org>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20200928113107.v2.1.I5e6f8c262031d0451fe7241b744f4f3111c1ce71@changeid
Signed-off-by: Matthias Brugger <matthias.bgg@gmail.com>

Here is the root cause:
The bug occurs because the system attempts to call `pm_genpd_init` with `is_off=false` even when a power domain fails to power on during boot. This leads to subsequent attempts to disable the power domain, resulting in warnings and potential issues due to disabled clocks being disabled again. The lack of proper error handling in the power-on process allows this situation to arise.

Here is the patch:
 
 static void mtk_register_power_domains(struct platform_device *pdev,
 				struct scp *scp, int num)
 {
 	struct genpd_onecell_data *pd_data;
 	int i, ret;
 
 	for (i = 0; i < num; i++) {
 		struct scp_domain *scpd = &scp->domains[i];
 		struct generic_pm_domain *genpd = &scpd->genpd;
+		bool on;
 
 		/*
 		 * Initially turn on all domains to make the domains usable
 		 * with !CONFIG_PM and to get the hardware in sync with the
 		 * software.  The unused domains will be switched off during
 		 * late_init time.
 		 */
-		genpd->power_on(genpd);
+		on = !WARN_ON(genpd->power_on(genpd) < 0);
 
-		pm_genpd_init(genpd, NULL, false);
+		pm_genpd_init(genpd, NULL, !on);
 	}
 
 	/*
 	 * We are not allowed to fail here since there is no way to unregister
 	 * a power domain. Once registered above we have to keep the domains
 	 * valid.
 	 */
 
 	pd_data = &scp->pd_data;
 
 	ret = of_genpd_add_provider_onecell(pdev->dev.of_node, pd_data);
 	if (ret)
 		dev_err(&pdev->dev, "Failed to add OF provider: %d\n", ret);
 }

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
genpd->power_on(genpd);
pm_genpd_init(genpd, NULL, false);
```
Reason:
The system calls `genpd->power_on(genpd)` to power on the domain, but if this call fails (returns a negative value), the subsequent call to `pm_genpd_init(genpd, NULL, false)` is made with `is_off` set to `false`. This results in the system trying to disable a power domain that was never successfully powered on, leading to warnings and potential issues with disabled clocks.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
on = !WARN_ON(genpd->power_on(genpd) < 0);
pm_genpd_init(genpd, NULL, !on);
```
Reason:
The patch introduces a check for the return value of `genpd->power_on(genpd)`. If it fails, `on` is set to `false`, which is then passed to `pm_genpd_init`. This ensures that if the power domain fails to power on, `pm_genpd_init` is called with `is_off` set to `true`, preventing the system from attempting to disable a power domain that was never successfully powered on, thus avoiding warnings and potential issues.

